units.title: Making Friends
units.intro: Grammar: subject–verb agreement (including neither/nor, either/or, together with) and the other parts of speech: adverbs, conjunctions, prepositions and interjections.

cards.title: Subject–verb agreement
rule: A singular subject takes a singular verb (*My friend **lives** here*); a plural subject takes a plural verb (*My friends **live** here*).
With **either ... or** and **neither ... nor**, the verb agrees with the **nearer** subject: *Neither the teacher nor the **students are** here.* / *Either the students or the **teacher is** here.*
**Together with, as well as, along with** do not change the subject: *The captain, together with his players, **is** coming.* **Each, every, everyone, nobody** take a singular verb.

examples.text: Neither Ali nor his brothers is at home.
examples.fix: Neither Ali nor his brothers are at home.

examples.text: The headmaster, as well as the teachers, was present.

cards.title: Step by step: present simple with he / she / it
cards.problem: Complete: "Every morning, my father ____ (drink) a cup of coffee."

steps.text: **Step 1: Find the time words.** *Every morning* = a habit → present simple.
**Step 2: Find the subject.** *my father* = he → add **-s** to the verb.

cards.title: Step by step: present continuous with a group noun
cards.problem: Complete: "Listen! The school choir ____ (sing) the national anthem right now."

steps.text: **Step 1: Find the time words.** *Listen!* and *right now* = happening now → present continuous (am/is/are + -ing).
**Step 2: Find the subject.** *The choir* = one group → singular → **is**.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: I ________ the main reason for his sudden decision to leave the scholarship program.
cards.why:
**Step 1:** *understand* is a **state verb** (a verb of thinking or feeling, not an action).

**Step 2:** State verbs do not take -ing: ✗ *am understanding*.

**Step 3:** Subject *I* → **understand** (no -s). So the answer is B.

**Tip:** State verbs (know, understand, like, want, believe, own) stay in the simple form: I understand, she knows.

**In Tigrinya:** 'Understand' (ምርዳእ) ሓደ ካብቶም ናይ ኣእምሮ ኩነታት ዝገልጹ ግሶች (state verbs) ስለ ዝኾነ፡ ቀጻሊ እዋን (continuous form) ክወስድ ኣይኽእልን እዩ። ኣብ ትግርኛ 'ይርድኣኒ ኣሎ' (ቀጻሊ ዝመስል) እንተበልና እኳ፡ ብእንግሊዘኛ ግን ወትሩ 'understand' (Option B) ጥራይ ኢና ክንጽሕፍ ዘለና።

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Samson as well as his two best friends _______ going to the library at the moment.
cards.why: When a subject is joined to another noun by phrases like 'as well as', 'along with', or 'together with', the verb agrees with the first subject. Here, 'Samson' is singular, so the verb must be singular ('is' or 'was'). The time marker 'at the moment' indicates the present continuous tense, making 'is' the correct choice.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: The police ________ investigating the robbery that occurred near the national bank.
cards.why:
**Step 1:** *police* means the police officers – it is always plural in English.

**Step 2:** Plural subject → plural verb: **are** investigating.

**Step 3:** Do not be tricked: *police* has no -s, but it is still plural.

**Tip:** Find the real subject (cover phrases like "of the students" or "with his friends") and make the verb agree with it.

**In Tigrinya:** 'Police' (ፖሊስ) ዝብል ስም ክትርእዮ ከለኻ ናይ ነጸላ (singular) ይመስል እምበር፡ ብሰዋስው ግን ወትሩ ብዙሕ ቁጽሪ (plural) ተገይሩ ስለ ዝውሰድ ድሕሪኡ ዝመጽእ ግሲ 'are' (Option B) ክኸውን ኣለዎ።

cards.title: Step by step: "the number of" + singular verb
cards.problem: Complete: "Since the library was repaired, the number of visitors ____ (increase) a lot."

steps.text: **Step 1: Find the real subject.** *the number* (of visitors) – one number → singular.
**Step 2: Choose the tense.** *Since…* means from then until now → present perfect.
**Step 3: Put it together.** singular + present perfect → **has increased** (not *have*).
**Remember:** *the number of* + singular verb; *a number of* (= many) + plural verb.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Each of the candidates who applied for the engineering position ________ a written test.
cards.why:
**Step 1:** The subject is **Each** (each one) → singular.

**Step 2:** Ignore *of the candidates who applied…* – it only describes *each*.

**Step 3:** Singular → **has to take**.

**Tip:** Find the real subject (cover phrases like "of the students" or "with his friends") and make the verb agree with it.

**In Tigrinya:** እቲ ዋና ባእታ 'Each' (ነፍሲ ወከፍ) ስለ ዝኾነ፡ ብሰዋስው ወግዒ ነጸላ (singular) እዩ። ስለዚ ምስኡ ዝኸይድ ነጸላ ግሲ 'has to take' (Option A) ክኸውን ኣለዎ። 'candidates' (ሕጹያት) ዝብል ቃል ብዙሕ ስለ ዝኾነ 'have' ምምራጽ ጌጋ እዩ።

cards.title: Step by step: "one of" + singular verb
cards.problem: Complete: "One of the biggest problems for school leavers ____ the cost of university."

steps.text: **Step 1: Find the real subject.** *One* (of the problems) → singular.
**Step 2: Cover the middle words.** *One … ____ the cost* → *One **is***.
**Step 3: Do not match the verb with *problems*.** That word is inside the phrase *of the biggest problems*.

cards.title: Step by step: a group noun + singular verb
cards.problem: Complete: "The board of directors, although they had different ideas, ____ finally agreed on the budget."

steps.text: **Step 1: Find the real subject.** *The board* – one group → singular.
**Step 2: Cover the extra words.** *of directors* and *although they had different ideas* do not change the subject.
**Step 3: Choose the verb.** *The board **has** finally agreed.*

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Neither the regional program coordinator nor the senior researchers ________ present at the emergency project meeting yesterday.
cards.why:
**Step 1:** With *neither … nor*, the verb agrees with the subject **nearest** to it.

**Step 2:** The nearest subject is *the senior researchers* (plural).

**Step 3:** *yesterday* → past → **were**.

**Tip:** Find the real subject (cover phrases like "of the students" or "with his friends") and make the verb agree with it.

**In Tigrinya:** ምሉእ ሓሳብ ብ 'Neither... nor' ክእሰር ከሎ፡ እቲ ግሲ ምስቲ ናብኡ ዝቐረበ ባእታ ይሰማማዕ (Proximity Rule)። እቲ ዝቐረበ ባእታ 'the senior researchers' (ብዙሕ) ስለ ዝኾነን እቲ ግዜ ድማ 'yesterday' (ትማሊ) ስለ ዝኾነን፡ ቅኑዕ መልሲ 'were' (Option B) እዩ።

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: The local police ________ currently searching the forest area for the prisoners who escaped from the regional jail.
cards.why:
**Step 1:** *police* is always plural.

**Step 2:** *currently* = now → present → **are** searching.

**Step 3:** *is* and *was* are singular; *were* is past.

**Tip:** Find the real subject (cover phrases like "of the students" or "with his friends") and make the verb agree with it.

**In Tigrinya:** 'Police' (ፖሊስ) ዝብል ስም ብቅርጹ ነጸላ ይመስል እምበር፡ ብሰዋስው ወግዒ ግን ወትሩ ብዙሕ ቁጽሪ (plural) እዩ። 'currently' (ኣብዚ እዋን) ዝብል ቃል ድማ ህልው እዋን ስለ ዝሕብር፡ ምስኡ ዝኸይድ ግሲ 'are' (Option B) እዩ።

cards.title: Parts of speech (2)
rule: An **adverb** describes a verb, adjective or another adverb (*She speaks **frankly***; *very* tall). Many adverbs = adjective + **-ly** (*happy → happily, easy → easily, late → lately* (= recently)). A **conjunction** joins (*and, because, although*). A **preposition** shows place, time or relation (*in, on, at, apart from*). An **interjection** shows feeling (*Oh! Wow! Ouch!*).

cards.problem: Find and correct the error: "She sings beautiful."

steps.text: **Step 1: Recall the rule for this pattern.**
**Step 2: Test the sentence.** "She sings beautiful." breaks this rule.

cards.title: Memory tip
body: **Nearer rules** for either/or and neither/nor; **ignore the extra** after together with / as well as.

cards.title: Unit summary
body: Singular subjects take singular verbs and plural subjects plural verbs. With either/or and neither/nor the verb agrees with the nearer subject; phrases like together with do not change the subject. Adverbs describe verbs (often -ly); prepositions, conjunctions and interjections complete the parts of speech.

cards.title: Step by step: Parts of speech (2) – making the verb agree
body: **Step 1:** Find the subject (a noun or pronoun) and decide if it is singular or plural.
**Step 2:** A singular subject in the present simple takes verb + -s: "The girl reads." A plural subject takes the base verb: "The girls read."
**Step 3:** Ignore phrases between the subject and the verb: "The list of names is long."
**Step 4:** Words like everybody, someone, each, nobody are singular: "Everybody has arrived."
**Step 5:** With either…or / neither…nor the verb agrees with the nearer subject; with "together with / as well as" the verb agrees with the first subject.

**Example:** "The teacher, together with her students, (visit/visits) the museum." First subject = the teacher (singular) → visits. "Either the boys or their father (is/are) at home." Nearer subject = father → is.

cards.title: Mnemonic — "One subject, one -s"
body: the -s goes on the noun OR on the verb, not both (the dog barks / the dogs bark).

cards.title: Exam tip
body: Underline the subject and draw an arrow to the verb before choosing – it stops you being misled by the noun closest to the verb.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: In "She answered the question correctly", what part of speech is "correctly"?
cards.why:
**Step 1:** "correctly" tells how she answered.

**Step 2:** Words that describe verbs are adverbs.

**Step 3:** So it is an adverb.

**Tip:** Ask what job the word does: names a thing → noun; describes a noun → adjective; tells how/when/where → adverb; shows place or time before a noun → preposition.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.why:
**Step 1:** The suffix -ous makes adjectives (famous, dangerous).

**Step 2:** "dangerously" is an adverb, "endanger" a verb, "dangers" a plural noun.

**Step 3:** So: dangerous.

**Tip:** Ask what job the word does: names a thing → noun; describes a noun → adjective; tells how/when/where → adverb; shows place or time before a noun → preposition.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: In "We walked across the bridge", which word is a preposition?
cards.why:
**Step 1:** A preposition shows a relationship of place, direction or time between words.

**Step 2:** "across" shows direction in relation to "the bridge".

**Step 3:** The other words are a verb, a noun and a pronoun.

**Tip:** Ask what job the word does: names a thing → noun; describes a noun → adjective; tells how/when/where → adverb; shows place or time before a noun → preposition.

glossary.meaning: The verb matches the subject in number.
A word that describes a verb, adjective or adverb.
